app.name: Freelief
app.tagline: You are safe right now. Take your time.
nav.label: Screens
nav.breatheHint: Follow the circle in and out.
nav.bubblesHint: Slow, soft bubbles. Pop as many as you like.
nav.traceHint: Follow a slow loop with your finger or the arrow keys.
nav.sortHint: Put soft colors in order, from light to dark.
nav.rippleHint: Touch still water and watch soft ripples spread.
nav.mandalaHint: Fill soft shapes with calm colors, at your own pace.
nav.calmHint: Slow music and soft shapes. Rest your eyes, or make the screen black.
breathe.title: Breathe
breathe.paused: Paused. Resume when you are ready.
bubbles.title: Pop bubbles
bubbles.intro: Tap a bubble, or move to one and press Enter. There is nothing to win.
trace.title: Trace a shape
trace.intro: Move the dot slowly around the loop with your finger, or with the arrow keys. Go at your own pace.
trace.oneLoop: One loop. Keep going for as long as you like.
trace.loops: {count} loops. Keep going for as long as you like.
calm.title: Visualizer
calm.intro: Slow music, soft rain, or both, with soft shapes. Nothing to do. Breathe, watch, or close your eyes.
calm.blackHint: The screen turns black and the sound keeps playing. Tap anywhere to bring it back.
calm.blackLabel: Black screen. Tap or press any key to bring the screen back.
calm.soundsOff: Sound is off. Use the speaker button at the top to hear it.
sort.title: Sort colors
sort.intro: Put the tiles in order, from lightest on the left to darkest on the right. Choose a tile, then choose the tile to swap it with, or drag a tile onto another. Arrow keys move between tiles.
sort.chosen: {name} chosen. Now choose the tile to swap it with.
sort.done: All in order, from lightest to darkest. Choose New colors for another set, or stay here.
ripple.title: Ripple pond
ripple.intro: Touch the water, or draw your finger across it, and soft ripples spread out. With a keyboard or screen reader, press the pond to make a ripple. There is nothing to win.
ripple.pondLabel: Pond. Press to make a ripple.
mandala.title: Color a mandala
mandala.intro: Choose a color, then tap a shape to fill it. With a keyboard, the arrow keys move around a ring and between rings, and Enter fills the shape. There is nothing to finish.
settings.title: Settings
settings.hapticsHint: A short buzz on taps. Android only (Chrome, Samsung Internet), not iPhone.
settings.regionHint: Need urgent help? opens on this region. It is saved only on this device. Freelief never asks for your location.
settings.updateHint: Gets the newest version from the internet and restarts Freelief. Your settings are kept.
settings.updateOffline: You need an internet connection to update.
settings.updating: Updating. Freelief will restart in a moment.
settings.updateFailed: Could not update. This version still works offline.
help.title: Urgent help
help.intro: If you might act on thoughts of harming yourself, or you are not safe, reach out now. These people are there to listen.
help.emergency: If you are in immediate danger, call {number}.
help.emergencyUnknown: If you are in immediate danger, call your local emergency number.
help.chatNote: Chat online needs an internet connection.
help.directory: Find a helpline in your country
help.directoryNote: {note} This link needs an internet connection.
footer.label: About Freelief
about.title: About Freelief
about.selfHelp1: Freelief is a free self-help tool for moments of panic or strong anxiety. It is not medical care. It does not diagnose or treat any condition, and it does not replace a doctor, a therapist or emergency services.
about.selfHelp2: If panic attacks happen often, or change how you live, please talk to a doctor or a mental health professional. Effective help exists.
about.selfHelp3: If you are in danger, or might harm yourself, use "Need urgent help?" at the top of every screen, or call your local emergency number.
about.privacy1: Freelief collects nothing about you. It has no account, no analytics and no advertising. Freelief sends nothing about you. The only thing that reaches the internet is your browser's check for a newer version of Freelief, from GitHub Pages.
about.privacy2: Freelief saves only the settings you change: your breathing rhythm, where it opens, sound, vibration, colors, the Visualizer's sound, and your country for urgent help. They stay on this device and are never sent anywhere. Clearing your browser data removes them.
about.open1: Freelief is free to use and its source code is open, under the MIT license.
standards.title: Standards and research
standards.verifiedIntro: Freelief meets these standards. Each one was checked by people, with a screen reader and with a keyboard only, for this version:
standards.none: Freelief is built to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA, and level AAA where it can. Automated accessibility checks run on every screen of every version. We do not claim a standard yet: a standard is shown here only after people check Freelief with a screen reader and with a keyboard only.
standards.help: You can help: check Freelief with your screen reader or keyboard and tell us what you find.
standards.researchIntro: Every exercise and activity in Freelief is based on published research, cited below. For some, the research is about something close to the activity, not the activity itself; each section says how strong the evidence is. No study has tested Freelief itself.
standards.evidence.breathing: Slow, steady breathing has been studied in randomized trials and reviews. Breathing at under 10 breaths a minute was linked with calmer body signals and less anxiety, mostly in healthy adults. All of Freelief's rhythms are this slow. In one trial of daily practice, a breathing method with a double breath in and a long breath out improved mood more than mindfulness did; box breathing was also tested there, but that trial did not compare the breathing methods with each other. A trial in people with panic disorder used a four-week breathing training that Freelief does not copy. No study has tested breathing during a panic attack with Freelief.
standards.evidence.bubbles: Turning your attention to something simple eased strong feelings a little, across many experiments, and a review found that ordinary video games can lower stress and anxiety. No study has tested this activity itself, and the evidence is limited.
standards.evidence.trace: A task that takes up your attention can make upsetting pictures in the mind feel less sharp. That research used eye movements while people recalled upsetting images, which is not the same as this activity. No study has tested this activity itself.
standards.evidence.sort: Simple visual puzzles, such as the game Tetris, use the same mental space as upsetting mental pictures, and in experiments they reduced intrusive memories after a distressing film. That research is about memories, not panic. No study has tested this activity itself.
standards.evidence.ripple: People tend to rate scenes with water as more restful, and in one small study people recovered from stress a little faster while hearing nature sounds. The evidence is limited and comes from photographs and recordings. No study has tested this activity itself.
standards.evidence.mandala: Small studies found that coloring a structured pattern, such as a mandala, lowered short-term anxiety after a mild stress. In one study a plaid pattern worked as well as a mandala; in others the mandala did better. The studies were small, and none was about a panic attack.
standards.evidence.calm: Across about a hundred randomized trials, listening to music lowered stress a little, in body and mind. The evidence for nature sounds such as rain is limited: one small study found faster recovery on one body measure. Freelief's rain is a gentle imitation, not a recording, and this visualizer has not been studied itself.
standards.evidence.distraction: Distraction can ease strong feelings for a short time. Some researchers think that always escaping anxiety can keep it going over time, although the evidence for that is mixed. Use these activities for the moment, and talk to a doctor or a mental health professional if panic comes back often.
feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.intro: Tell us what works, what does not, and how Freelief works with your screen reader or keyboard. Nothing is sent by Freelief itself: you read and edit the message, copy it, and paste it into GitHub yourself.
feedback.kind: What would you like to send?
feedback.messageLabel: Your message (you can change all of it)
feedback.danger: Feedback is not watched around the clock. If you are in danger now, use "Need urgent help?" at the top, or call your local emergency number.
feedback.copied: Copied. Now open GitHub and paste it into the issue.
feedback.copyFailed: Could not copy. The message is selected: copy it yourself, then paste it into the issue.
feedback.githubNote: Opens a new issue on GitHub. Paste your message there. GitHub issues are public: please do not include health or personal details. GitHub needs a free account.
feedback.emailNote: Opens your email app with this message filled in.
